newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: GES Singapore in back door listing in Australia.
newsitem.headline: GES Singapore in back door listing in Australia.

text.p: GES Singapore Pte Ltd said on Tuesday it will enter into a share swap agreement with Australia's Logiciel International Ltd (LIL) giving it a back door listing on the Australian Stock Exchange.
A GES statement said under the agreement, the vendors of GES will sell to LIL 2.15 million GES shares representing 100 percent of the company for Singapore $56 million.
In return, LIL, which is incorporated in Singapore, will issue to the vendors of GES 243.5 million new LIL shares, representing about 85.1 percent of the company at Singapore $0.23 cents each.
In accordance to the Singapore takeover code, the vendors through Alxia Pte Ltd will make a takeover offer for the remaining LIL shares they do not own.
It said the formal takeover offer is expected to be made next week.

LIL's principal shareholders OCBC, Wearnes & Walden Investments (Singapore) Ltd and Gainall Pte Ltd, who hold a total of 17.1 percent of the company, have told Alxia that they will retain their holdings in the company.
GES makes computers and computer related products under its own Datamini brand as well as provide manufacturing services to original equipment manufacturers (OEM).
For the year ended December 1995, the group made net profit of Singapore $8.3 million.

"The listing exercise is part of the group's plans to manage its rapid growth in the IT (information technology) industry in the region and around the world," said GES chairman Goh Lik Tuan in the statement.
